shots.alt: The session screen immediately after launch, showing READY, Another Last Dance, Sandy Boys, 240 BPM, and the message Press Play to prepare the music with these settings.
shots.caption: On launch the bundled default dance and tune are ready; press Play to render the music.

shots.alt: The Select dance screen with a saved-dance search field, a folder sidebar listing Warmups and Encores, three saved cards, and Another Last Dance selected for preview.
shots.caption: Select dance lists your saved cards; search them, group them into folders, and load one without a network.

shots.alt: The Select dance screen with belle typed in the saved-dance search, the Warmups folder selected, one matching card, and its preview.
shots.caption: Saved content is searched locally; the folder panel filters the list and offers rename and delete.

shots.alt: The Select tune screen with a saved-tune search field, a folder sidebar listing Reels and Jigs, three saved tunes, and Sandy Boys sheet music.
shots.caption: Select tune lists your saved tunes with an offline sheet-music preview.

shots.alt: The Select tune screen with saint typed in the saved-tune search, the Reels folder selected, one matching tune, and its sheet music.
shots.caption: The same saved-content search and folders apply to tunes.

shots.alt: The About category of the Preferences screen, showing Caller Karaoke, its version, a short description, By Nicholas Gower, and links to the website and the source code.
shots.caption: About is one of the Preferences categories, beside the settings list.

shots.alt: The Dance glossary reference page with a filter field, a source link, a scrolling list of contra dance terms, and the Balance and swing entry boxed with an emphasis border.
shots.caption: The in-app glossary is its own tab, opens at a linked term, and works offline.

shots.alt: The session screen with a definition tooltip beside the hovered Balance and swing term, naming the term and explaining the balance-then-swing figure.
shots.caption: Hovering a linked term on a desktop, or resting a finger on it on a phone, shows its short definition.

shots.alt: The Download dance screen with a Dance source menu above Title, Choreographer, User, Hook, Formation, Figure type, Figure contains, Verified only, and Sort fields, above an empty results area.
shots.caption: Download dance selects its source and searches it, then previews a card before saving it locally.

shots.alt: The Download dance screen with last typed in the Title field, a list of matching dances on the left with downloaded badges, and the preview pane on the right.
shots.caption: Results show the title, choreographer, and formation; Preview opens the figures.

shots.alt: The Download dance screen with Another Last Dance selected, the Download again, Use this dance, and View saved dances buttons, and its figure list below.
shots.caption: Download the card for offline use or load it immediately; either action saves it to your library.

shots.alt: The session screen after choosing Another Last Dance, showing its title, figures, and tune summary in the dance card and the prompt ready to play.
shots.caption: Using a dance returns to the session and marks the music for a rebuild.

shots.alt: The Download tune screen with Search and Composer fields, Key, Meter, and Genre menus, and an empty results area.
shots.caption: Download tune searches ABC Session Tunes and previews the sheet music.

shots.alt: The Download tune preview showing the tune metadata, credits, source link, Show ABC toggle, Download again and Use this tune buttons, and rendered sheet music.
shots.caption: The preview engraves the ABC as sheet music; Download saves it and Use loads it.

shots.alt: The session controls with the Tempo slider set to 240 BPM beside one Play/Pause button, Restart, End tune, Loop, Cycle tunes, Count-in, Speak calls, and Volume.
shots.caption: Tempo changes mark the music for a rebuild; press Play to apply them.

shots.alt: The session screen during the count-in, showing a large 2, the label COUNT-IN, and either CALL NOW with the first call or Listen for the first chord.
shots.caption: The four-beat count-in sets the tempo before the 64-beat loop begins.

shots.alt: The session screen showing a length-check warning that the dance and tune lengths differ, above the dance card.
shots.caption: The session warns when the dance and tune lengths differ; it does not rescale either one.

shots.alt: The session screen during a figure, showing the CALL NOW prompt, the executes-in countdown, the NEXT footer naming the following call inside the same card, and the active dance-card row.
shots.caption: The large prompt is the call to say now; its footer previews the next call, so the panel keeps one height.

shots.alt: The session screen showing the message Playback settings will apply without restarting; press Play to apply them now, with the current call still visible.
shots.caption: Playback settings apply without restarting; press Play to apply them immediately.

shots.alt: The session screen while a figure is being danced, showing the UPCOMING MOVE prompt naming the next call and the beats until it starts.
shots.caption: While dancers execute a figure, the prompt switches to the move the caller must say next.

shots.alt: The session screen with playback paused, the current musical position retained, and the Play control available.
shots.caption: Pause stops the music and any speech; Play resumes from the same position.

shots.alt: The session screen after the non-looping dance ends, showing the message Dance complete and the instruction to press Restart.
shots.caption: With looping off, the session stops at the end of the loop.

shots.alt: The session screen during the slow ending, showing SLOW FINISH, the tune title, the message Slowing down and holding the last note, and a full progress bar.
shots.caption: End tune eases the last four beats, thins the band, holds the final chord a fifth below, and then stops.

shots.alt: The session controls with Cycle tunes on, the tune-set line naming the next tune and the change interval, and the Change tune every slider.
shots.caption: Cycle tunes changes to the next saved tune at a repeat, using music rendered during the previous pass.

shots.alt: The Select tune screen with one saved tune marked In set and another offering Add to set, beside the tune-set hint.
shots.caption: Add saved tunes to the set; Cycle tunes then plays them in turn.

shots.alt: The Preferences screen opened from the gear button in the top-right corner, which the focus ring marks, with the Calling, Band & Sound, Playback, Appearance, Data & Storage, and About categories in a left column.
shots.caption: The gear opens Preferences; categories keep settings in one place, and playback changes apply without restarting.

shots.alt: The Preferences screen with a numbered focus ring on the Preferences gear button in the top-right corner, another on Calling in the category list, and another on the Edit dance move aliases button under Role terms.
shots.caption: The gear opens Preferences; select Calling, then Edit dance move aliases to change the call words.

shots.alt: The Role terms section with the Larks / Robins preset selected (presets read left side first) and the live role-replacement example below it.
shots.caption: Presets name the left side first; Larks / Robins is the default and the example updates as the terms change.

shots.alt: The Role terms section with the Custom preset selected and Left singular, Left plural, Right singular, and Right plural fields.
shots.caption: Custom terms replace role words in both the card and the calls.

shots.alt: The Appearance category of Preferences, showing the Theme buttons, the Interface section with Smooth animations, Dance card padding, and Show dance glossary, the Undo and Redo buttons, and the keyboard shortcut reference.
shots.caption: Appearance settings control theme, screen transitions, dance card spacing, the glossary, undo and redo, and the keyboard shortcuts.

shots.alt: The session screen with a dance card and call prompt using the chosen role terms instead of ladles and gentlespoons.
shots.caption: Role terms are applied to the card and to the rendered calls.

shots.alt: The Dance move aliases screen with a Filter field, the Reset all aliases button, and a long list of move types with editable alias templates.
shots.caption: Each recognised move type has an alias template; overridden entries are marked.

shots.alt: The Dance move aliases screen with the Swing row focused and its alias template selected for editing.
shots.caption: Edit the words shown and spoken for a move type.

shots.alt: The top of the Dance move aliases screen showing the supported placeholders: actor, actor_singular, actor_plural, actor_object, actor_object_plural, direction, and count.
shots.caption: Placeholders are filled from the card phrase; unknown placeholders are left as text.

shots.alt: The Custom figure aliases section with a card phrase field, a call-to-say field, and the Add alias button.
shots.caption: Use a custom alias when the classifier does not recognise a figure phrase.

shots.alt: The session screen showing a custom or edited alias in the current-call prompt and the dance card.
shots.caption: Alias changes rebuild the call timeline and move calls earlier or later as the wording changes.

shots.alt: Band & Sound showing the default band list: Melody · Fiddle with two players, Accompaniment · Piano, Countermelody · Fiddle with two players, and Percussion · Foot taps with three players, each row with its part, instrument, players, direction, volume, and Remove/Up/Down controls, with Add instrument below.
shots.caption: The default band is two melody fiddles, a piano, two countermelody fiddles, and three foot taps.

shots.alt: Band & Sound with the Accompaniment row changed to Guitar and two players, above the Countermelody and Percussion rows, with the Boom-chuck accompaniment rhythm below the list.
shots.caption: Any voice can take any part: a guitar accompaniment is its own row with its own players, level, and place.

shots.alt: Band & Sound with the Countermelody row set to Fiddle and two players, above the Percussion row.
shots.caption: A countermelody row adds a second line without copying the melody row; the default is two countermelody fiddles.

shots.alt: Band & Sound with the Percussion row set to Foot taps and two players, the Percussion rhythm menu set to Gallop, and the optional note below the band list.
shots.caption: Percussion is a band row: Foot taps play a one-and-a gallop, Drumset adds a full kit, and the rhythm menu changes the pattern.

shots.alt: Band & Sound showing the dancer sounds toggle and volume, the percussion and accompaniment rhythm menus, and the separate Caller volume and Band volume sliders.
shots.caption: The caller and the band have independent levels; dancer sounds are temporarily disabled while their rhythms are corrected.

shots.alt: The Playback section showing the master Vary the music and Humanize the band checkboxes with their per-kind options, timing and tuning sliders, fiddle bowing rules, and the gradual-ending checkboxes.
shots.caption: Music variations, fiddle bowing, and humanizing each expose their parts; the fiddle drifts in intonation and the ending eases in before resolving a fifth below.

shots.alt: The Soundfont section showing a loaded SoundFont name, the Load .sf2 button, and the Use bundled button.
shots.caption: A user-supplied SoundFont replaces the bundled instrument voices.

shots.alt: The Soundfont section showing Bundled: Fluid R3 GM and the Load .sf2 button.
shots.caption: Use bundled returns the session to the packaged instruments.

shots.alt: The Soundfont section with a red error message below the current SoundFont name.
shots.caption: An unreadable or unsupported SoundFont leaves the previous instrument setup in place.

shots.alt: The Calling lead section with Automatic syllable-based lead turned on, the minimum, maximum, and speech rate sliders, the safety padding, and the Rebuild call timing button.
shots.caption: Automatic lead derives the call time from the rendered words.

shots.alt: The Calling lead section showing Minimum speech lead and Maximum speech lead sliders, the Speech rate slider, and the safety padding note.
shots.caption: The speech lead is clamped to one to five beats; the safety padding is added and the total rounds up to a whole beat.

shots.alt: The Calling lead section with the Speech rate slider showing syllables per second and the safety padding note.
shots.caption: A lower speech rate moves longer calls earlier.

shots.alt: The Calling lead section with the Rebuild call timing button below the lead controls.
shots.caption: Rebuild the timeline after changing lead settings if the session does not do it automatically.

shots.alt: The session screen with the CALL NOW prompt and the executes-in countdown showing how many beats remain before the dancers move.
shots.caption: Calls start before the execute beat so the words finish before the move.

shots.alt: The session screen during the count-in with the first call previewed below Listen for the first chord.
shots.caption: The first call can begin during the count-in because it starts before beat zero.

shots.alt: The Text to speech section showing the Kokoro Voice selector, the voice description, the Rate slider, the Tone selector, the Deliveries per call slider, and the headless-ready status line.
shots.caption: Desktop and Android use a local Kokoro voice; rate, tone, and deliveries per call change the spoken delivery without changing visual timing.

shots.alt: The Text to speech section showing the Speak calls checkbox and a muted message explaining that TTS is unavailable.
shots.caption: If the system has no speech voice, visual calls still work.

shots.alt: The Maintenance section with Clear source cache replaced by Confirm clear cache and Cancel buttons.
shots.caption: Clearing the cache is a two-step action.

shots.alt: The Maintenance section after clearing the cache, with the status Cache cleared shown below the buttons.
shots.caption: Clearing the source cache does not remove saved dances, tunes, or the bundled defaults.

shots.alt: The Web data proxy section with Proxy URL and Token fields and the note that it is only needed by the web build.
shots.caption: Desktop and Android fetch sources directly; the web build can use a proxy.

shots.alt: The Theme section with Light selected and the surrounding Preferences screen rendered in warm cream.
shots.caption: The light theme keeps the same neutral structure in a warm cream palette.

shots.alt: The session screen in the light theme, with dark text on a warm cream background and the current call highlighted.
shots.caption: The light theme is available for bright rooms and projectors.

shots.alt: The Maintenance section with the Export MIDI button, the Clear source cache button, the status line, and the Memory use table.
shots.caption: MIDI export is desktop-only in 0.1.0; clearing cache works on every platform, and Memory use lists the largest resident allocations.

shots.alt: The Download dance screen with a red source error in the bottom panel and a Dismiss button.
shots.caption: A failed search or detail request leaves the current dance and tune in place.

shots.alt: The Download tune screen with a red message that a source response could not be parsed and a Dismiss button.
shots.caption: A short reason is shown; the current content is not replaced.

shots.alt: The session controls with a red Audio device message below the transport row.
shots.caption: Without an output device the app falls back to a silent engine; restore audio and restart.

shots.alt: The Download dance Sort menu set to Title A–Z.
shots.caption: Sorting applies the next time Search dances runs.

shots.alt: The bottom of the Download dance screen with Previous, Page 1 of 12, and Next controls.
shots.caption: Results are shown ten at a time.

shots.alt: A dance preview showing a figure count and a total that is not 64 beats.
shots.caption: The card can total fewer or more than 64 beats; the music keeps its 64-beat grid.

shots.alt: The Download dance screen with an error in the bottom panel after a failed search or preview.
shots.caption: Dismiss the error and retry, or use a cached result if one is available.

shots.alt: The Download tune screen with a search term and a list of matching tunes with title, composer, key, and meter.
shots.caption: Search matches title and composer; filters narrow the result set.

shots.alt: The Download tune screen with Key set to A mixolydian and matching results.
shots.caption: The key menu uses a curated list of common contra keys.

shots.alt: The Download tune screen with Meter set to 4/4 and matching results.
shots.caption: Meter filters the ABC Session Tunes results before searching.

shots.alt: The Download tune screen with Genre set to reel and matching results.
shots.caption: Genre is the ABC Session Tunes rhythm field.

shots.alt: The Download tune screen with an error in the bottom panel after a failed search or preview.
shots.caption: The current tune stays loaded if a new one cannot be fetched or parsed.

shots.alt: The session controls with the Loop checkbox cleared.
shots.caption: With looping off, the dance stops at the end of the 64-beat loop.

shots.alt: The session controls with the Volume slider visible beside the transport buttons.
shots.caption: Master volume is separate from the melody and accompaniment balances in Preferences.

shots.alt: The tune and instrument summary below the call prompt, showing the tune title, key, rhythm, melody, accompaniment, countermelody, and percussion with its rhythm, and the copy counts for each part.
shots.caption: The summary confirms what will play before you start.

shots.alt: The session controls with the Speak calls checkbox selected.
shots.caption: Spoken calls accompany the visual prompt; the visual prompt is never hidden.

shots.alt: The session screen at phone width with one-row tabs, full-width Tempo, Caller, and Band sliders whose rails sit inside rounded outlines with padlocks, Play/Pause, Restart, and End on one row, and a green CALL NOW prompt above the dance card.
shots.caption: The phone layout gives the sliders the full width and every control a 44-pixel touch target; each rail is outlined with a padlock until the slider is tapped.

shots.alt: The session screen in a 390-pixel-wide window with compact tabs, outlined and padlocked Tempo, Caller, and Band sliders, stacked transport controls, the READY prompt, and the dance card below.
shots.caption: The compact layout keeps every session control usable at phone width, with outlined sliders guarded until tapped.

shots.alt: An alias row with the Reset to default button highlighted.
shots.caption: Resetting one alias restores the built-in wording for that move.

shots.alt: The Dance move aliases header with the Reset all aliases button.
shots.caption: Reset all aliases returns every move type to its default template.

shots.alt: The Download dance screen with a User filter entered and matching results.
shots.caption: With ContraDB selected, the User filter matches the contributor name.

shots.alt: The Download dance screen with a Hook filter entered and matching results.
shots.caption: With ContraDB selected, the Hook filter matches the short hook line on its cards.

shots.alt: The Download dance Figure menu set to Swing, above the matching results.
shots.caption: Figure type sends a move-type filter and takes precedence over Figure contains.

shots.alt: The GitHub release page with the Windows setup executable and portable ZIP listed as assets.
shots.caption: Download the setup program or portable ZIP from the latest release.

shots.alt: The Inno Setup installer wizard for Caller Karaoke showing the Select Destination Location page, the C:\Program Files\Caller Karaoke folder, and the Next button.
shots.caption: Follow the wizard, choose whether to create a desktop shortcut, and finish.

shots.alt: The Windows SmartScreen warning for an unsigned installer, with the More info link visible.
shots.caption: Only run the unsigned build if it came from this repository.

shots.alt: A file-manager view of the extracted portable ZIP folder with caller-karaoke.exe listed beside the license, readme, credits, and changelog files.
shots.caption: The portable build runs from its folder and does not write to the registry.

shots.alt: The Downloads folder in the Nemo file manager on Linux Mint with caller-app_0.2.1-1_amd64.deb selected, showing 31.8 MB, Archive, and -rw-rw-r-- permissions.
shots.caption: Install the .deb with apt so dependencies are resolved.

shots.alt: The Downloads folder in Nemo with CallerKaraoke-0.2.1-x86_64.AppImage selected, showing 39.0 MB, Program, and executable -rwxrwxr-x permissions.
shots.caption: Run the AppImage directly, or use --appimage-extract-and-run without FUSE.

shots.alt: The Caller Karaoke browser build open in a tab with the session screen and a Play button.
shots.caption: Serve the bundle over HTTP and press Play once to allow audio.

shots.alt: The Android package-installer confirmation for the Caller Karaoke APK, including the unknown-apps prompt.
shots.caption: Android may require permission to install apps from this source.

shots.alt: The Caller Karaoke app open on an Android device showing the session screen.
shots.caption: The Android build is still being device-tested.
